query: One Evening's Work Every notice says "from next term", except one, pinned low and crooked: {~the refectory wants hands for the end-of-term clear-out|the porters want someone to carry exam desks back to the store rooms|a professor wants her rooms boxed up before the break}. One evening, paid on the night. Take the evening's work {~You scrub, carry and stack until the lamps go out. The pay is counted into your hand, coin by coin, by someone too tired to talk.|It is heavier work than the card let on. Your arms ache all the next day, and your purse is heavier for it.|You finish late, sore and paid. Nobody remembers your name, which is the restful part.} Leave it for someone else {~You leave the card where it is. Somebody poorer will want it more, and you want your evening.|You read it twice and walk on. The term is nearly over; so is your patience for work.|You let the card be. The evening goes on a long walk instead, which pays nothing and feels like a lot.}
